scene_translation: The woman had slipped into a small coffee shop at the end of the alley. When Testo cautiously pushed the door open, the smell of coffee and old wood drifted out. The woman was seated at the far end of the counter and, without even glancing over, said: "I knew you'd come, Testo. Have you read that notebook yet?" The old man who seemed to be the owner quietly polished a cup behind the counter and shot Testo a brief sideways look.
grammar_note: 【～もせずに】meaning "without even ~ing" — a stronger way to say "without doing" than just ～ないで. Here, 見もせずに means "without even looking". The も adds emphasis: not just that she didn't look, but she didn't so much as glance. Pattern: verb stem + もせずに.

vocab.meaning: dead end, the very end of a path
proprietor of a small bar or café
a fleeting glance, a quick look
the back, the interior (of a room or space)

mystery_memo: The woman in the blue raincoat has led Testo to a retro coffee shop at the end of the alley — clearly a place she knows well, possibly her base. She again uses Testo's name with familiarity and references the unlabeled notebook, implying she knows Testo has it. She is confident and slightly ahead of Testo at every step — relationship: mysterious/neutral, not yet hostile. The old master of the café noticed Testo with quiet wariness — possible recurring NPC. The notebook is the central item: the woman's question implies it contains something that should already mean something to Testo. NPC relationship status — blue raincoat woman: intriguing/slightly unsettling; café master: watchful/unknown.
